Isaiah 18 · Woe to the Land Shadowing with Wings

points: "Woe to the land shadowing with wings which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia." This is the reference to the land of Assyria, that sends ambassadors by the sea, even in vessels of bulrushes upon the water.

note.label: Isaiah 18: Woe to the Land Shadowing with Wings

points: The message goes to a nation scattered and peeled, a people terrible from their beginning, a nation meted out and trodden down whose land the rivers have spoiled.

note.label: Isaiah 18: Woe to the Land Shadowing with Wings

points: All the inhabitants of the world and dwellers on the earth are called to see when the ensign is lifted up on the mountains and to hear when the trumpet is blown.

note.label: Isaiah 18: Woe to the Land Shadowing with Wings

points: The Most High said He would take His rest and consider upon His dwelling place, like a clear heat upon herbs and like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.

note.label: Isaiah 18: Woe to the Land Shadowing with Wings

points: Before the harvest He cuts off the sprigs with pruning hooks and takes away and cuts down the branches, left together to the fowls of the mountains and the beasts of the earth to summer and winter upon.

note.label: Isaiah 18: Woe to the Land Shadowing with Wings

points: In that time the present shall be brought to the Most High of hosts, of a people scattered and peeled, to the place of the name of the Most High of hosts, the mount Zion.
